text:
mike: Quick sync — proposing a "minimal assertion" instrumentation pattern for edge proxies to stabilize cost attribution and SLO signals. Short version: require a tiny canonical set of fields at ingress (trace_id, service, route, billing_key if available, latency_ms) and add an optional lightweight assertion header for downstream hops. This keeps payloads small and makes late-enrichment easier.

anita: SGTM. Can you paste the exact minimal schema? we should be explicit so SDKs and nginx sidecars can adopt it.

mike: sure — example payload we want to assert at the edge (one-liner JSON for readability):
```json
{
  "trace_id":"<hex>",
  "service":"edge-proxy",
  "route":"/v1/generate",
  "billing_key":"acct_12345",
  "latency_ms":23
}
```

cheng: a couple tradeoffs:
- requiring billing_key everywhere is ideal for cost; but many internal clients won't have it. fallback rules needed.
- sampling interacts with assertions: if we sample aggressively, we must still keep a small deterministic subset that always carries billing_key for cost accuracy.

sam: fallback idea: if billing_key is missing, derive from route->team mapping at ingress and tag with "billing_key:derived:<team>" plus a low-confidence flag. better than leaving gaps. cost reports can mark derived vs asserted.

jin: +1 for derived, but be careful about duplicates for shared routes. Suggest we add an "assertion_source" enum header: `asserted|derived|late_enriched` so downstream pipelines can discount.

anita: how do we enforce this? runtime check in edge proxy + metrics emitted when assertion missing? we need both blocking and non-blocking modes for ramp.

mike: enforcement plan: 1) start with a non-blocking mode that emits a new metric `obs.assertion.missing{service=edge-proxy,route=...}` and increments a counter; 2) create an alert when missing_rate > 5% over 5m for a given route; 3) after 2 weeks and owners fix gaps, flip to blocking (HTTP 422) for high-traffic public routes only.

cheng: sampling note: we should attach a tiny hash field `assertion_hash` computed from trace_id+billing_key so we can detect downstream strip/dup without carrying full payload. cheap and helps reconciliation.

mike: good call. add `assertion_hash` to the minimal set. also propose header names for minimal adoption: `X-RW-Trace-Id`, `X-RW-Billing-Key`, `X-RW-Assertion-Source`, `X-RW-Assertion-Hash`.

sam: SDK/sidecar implementation note: we can add an opt-in fast path that populates headers at the TLS termination layer for older services. avoids modifying app code.

jin: ops playbook: run `obs.assertion.missing` per route; team owner gets a ticket automatically if missing_rate spikes. we can reuse existing oncall rotations.

observability-bot: canary check failed: one canary service (svc-canary-5) emitted 12% missing assertions in the last 10m. link: https://go/reports/assertion-canary

mike: ack — I'll take the ticket. action items:
- mike: draft short RFC with schema + headers + enforcement timeline (today)
- anita + sam: add sidecar opt-in path + nginx snippet (this sprint)
- cheng + jin: add metric names + alert rules to SLO runbook (this sprint)

anita: thanks — let's avoid creating new cardinality on metrics. use labels service/route/assertion_source only. no free-form keys.

mike: yup — keep labels small. we'll iterate on the RFC and post for review by EOD. :thumbsup:
